subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider `api_error: Internal server error` be classified for cron/fallback behavior: `server_error`, `overloaded`, `timeout`, or a cron-local transient class?
rationale: The current code makes this more than a regex gap because each class changes retry matching, fallback short-circuiting, and whether shared auth-profile health is affected.

options.title: Use cron-local server outage semantics
options.body: Treat the plain provider 500 shape as retryable provider outage for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy, and require tests proving fast-fail plus retry/failure-alert behavior.

options.title: Map it to overloaded
options.body: Skip same-provider profiles sooner through overload behavior, accepting the risk that broad HTTP 500 text can cool down healthy profiles if the match is too wide.

options.title: Defer to broader guardrails
options.body: Keep timeout-style classification for now and solve it only as part of a wider reason-aware cron guard and stream-stall budgeting design.

recommendation.title: Use cron-local server outage semantics
recommendation.body: Treat the plain provider 500 shape as retryable provider outage for cron/fallback without marking shared auth profiles unhealthy, and require tests proving fast-fail plus retry/failure-alert behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: altaywtf has the strongest recent history on structured server-error retry, overloaded failover, and the merged partial implementation.
